1.title: Getting to Know You
targets: I can tell statistical questions from non-statistical questions and can explain the difference.
I can tell the difference between numerical and categorical data.

2.title: Data Representations
targets: I can find the five-number summary for data.
I can use a dot plot, histogram, or box plot to represent data.

3.title: A Gallery of Data
targets: I can graphically represent the data that I collected and critique the representations of others’ data.

4.title: The Shape of Distributions
targets: I can use a graphical representation of data to suggest a situation that produced the data pictured.
I can use the terms "symmetric," "skewed," "uniform," "bimodal," and "bell-shaped" to describe the shape of a distribution.

5.title: Calculating Measures of Center and Variability
targets: I can calculate mean absolute deviation, interquartile range, mean, and median for a set of data.

6.title: Mystery Computations
targets: I can determine basic relationships between cell values in a spreadsheet by changing the values and noticing what happens in another cell.

7.title: Spreadsheet Computations
targets: I can use a spreadsheet as a calculator to find solutions to word problems.

8.title: Spreadsheet Shortcuts
targets: I can use shortcuts to fill in cells on a spreadsheet.

9.title: Technological Graphing
targets: I can use technology to create graphic representations of data and calculate statistics.

10.title: The Effect of Extremes
targets: I can describe how an extreme value will affect the mean and median.
I can use the shape of a distribution to compare the mean and median.

11.title: Comparing and Contrasting Data Distributions
targets: I can arrange data sets in order of variability, given graphic representations.

12.title: Standard Deviation
targets: I can describe standard deviation as a measure of variability.
I can use technology to compute standard deviation.

13.title: More Standard Deviation
targets: I can use standard deviation to say something about a situation.

14.title: Outliers
targets: I can find values that are outliers, investigate their source, and figure out what to do with them.
I can tell how an outlier affects mean, median, IQR, or standard deviation.

15.title: Comparing Data Sets
targets: I can compare and contrast situations using measures of center and measures of variability.

16.title: Analyzing Data
targets: I can collect data from an experiment and compare the results using measures of center and measures of variability.

1.title: Planning a Party
targets: I can explain the meaning of the term “constraints.”
I can tell which quantities in a situation can vary and which ones cannot.
I can use letters and numbers to write expressions representing the quantities in a situation.

2.title: Writing Equations to Model Relationships (Part 1)
targets: I can tell which quantities in a situation can vary and which ones cannot.
I can use letters and numbers to write equations representing the relationships in a situation.

3.title: Writing Equations to Model Relationships (Part 2)
targets: I can use words and equations to describe the patterns I see in a table of values or in a set of calculations.
When given a description of a situation, I can use representations like diagrams and tables to help make sense of the situation and write equations for it.

4.title: Equations and Their Solutions
targets: I can explain what it means for a value or pair of values to be a solution to an equation.
I can find solutions to equations by reasoning about a situation or by using algebra.

5.title: Equations and Their Graphs
targets: I can use graphing technology to graph linear equations and identify solutions to the equations.
I understand how the coordinates of the points on the graph of a linear equation are related to the equation.
When given the graph of a linear equation, I can explain the meaning of the points on the graph in terms of the situation it represents.

6.title: Equivalent Equations
targets: I can tell whether two expressions are equivalent and explain why or why not.
I know and can identify the moves that can be made to transform an equation into an equivalent one.
I understand what it means for two equations to be equivalent, and how equivalent equations can be used to describe the same situation in different ways.

7.title: Explaining Steps for Rewriting Equations
targets: I can explain why some algebraic moves create equivalent equations but some do not.
I know how equivalent equations are related to the steps of solving equations.
I know what it means for an equation to have no solutions and can recognize such an equation.

8.title: Which Variable to Solve for? (Part 1)
targets: Given an equation, I can solve for a particular variable (like height, time, or length) when the equation would be more useful in that form.
I know the meaning of the phrase “to solve for a variable.”

9.title: Which Variable to Solve for? (Part 2)
targets: I can write an equation to describe a situation that involves multiple quantities whose values are not known, and then solve the equation for a particular variable.
I know how solving for a variable can be used to quickly calculate the values of that variable.

10.title: Connecting Equations to Graphs (Part 1)
targets: I can describe the connections between an equation of the form ax+by=c, the features of its graph, and the rate of change in the situation.

11.title: Connecting Equations to Graphs (Part 2)
targets: I can find the slope and vertical intercept of a line with equation ax+by=c.

12.title: Writing and Graphing Systems of Linear Equations
targets: I can explain what we mean by “the solution to a system of linear equations” and can explain how the solution is represented graphically.
I can explain what we mean when we refer to two equations as a system of equations.
I can use tables and graphs to solve systems of equations.

13.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
targets: I can solve systems of equations by substituting a variable or an expression.
I know more than one way to perform substitution and can decide which way or what to substitute based on how the given equations are written.

14.title: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 1)
targets: I can solve systems of equations by adding or subtracting them to eliminate a variable.
I know that adding or subtracting equations in a system creates a new equation, where one of the solutions to this equation is the solution to the system.

15.title: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 2)
targets: I can explain why adding or subtracting two equations that share a solution results in a new equation that also shares the same solution.

16.title: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 3)
targets: I can solve systems of equations by multiplying each side of one or both equations by a factor, then adding or subtracting the equations to eliminate a variable.
I understand that multiplying each side of an equation by a factor creates an equivalent equation whose graph and solutions are the same as that of the original equation.

17.title: Systems of Linear Equations and Their Solutions
targets: I can tell how many solutions a system has by graphing the equations or by analyzing the parts of the equations and considering how they affect the features of the graphs.
I know the possibilities for the number of solutions a system of equations could have.

18.title: Asking about Solving Systems
targets: I can get more information about a problem in order to write and solve a system of linear equations.

19.title: Linear Patterns
targets: I can solve linear equations algebraically.
I can write linear equations to create a pattern.

1.title: Two-Way Tables
targets: I can calculate missing values in a two-way table.
I can create a two-way table for categorical data given information about a situation.
I can describe what the values in a two-way table mean in the context of the situation.

2.title: Relative Frequency Tables
targets: I can calculate values in a relative frequency table and describe what the values mean in everyday language.

3.title: Associations in Categorical Data
targets: I can look for patterns in two-way tables and relative frequency tables to see if there is a possible association between two variables.

4.title: Linear Models
targets: I can describe the rate of change and y-intercept for a linear model that represents a situation.
I can draw a linear model that fits the data well and use the linear model to estimate values I want to find.

5.title: Fitting Lines
targets: I can describe the rate of change and y-intercept for a linear model that represents a situation.
I can use technology to find the line of best fit.

6.title: Residuals
targets: I can plot and calculate residuals for a data set and use the information to judge whether a linear model is a good fit.

7.title: The Correlation Coefficient
targets: I can describe the goodness of fit of a linear model using the correlation coefficient.
I can match the correlation coefficient with a scatter plot and linear model.

8.title: Using the Correlation Coefficient
targets: I can describe the strength of a relationship between two variables.
I can use technology to find the correlation coefficient and explain what the value tells me about a linear model that represents a situation.

9.title: Causal Relationships
targets: I can look for connections between two variables to analyze whether or not there is a causal relationship.

10.title: Fossils and Flags
targets: I can collect data, create a linear model to fit the data, determine if the linear model is a good fit, and use the information from my linear model to answer questions.

1.title: Representing Situations with Inequalities
targets: I can write inequalities that represent the constraints in a situation.

2.title: Solutions to Inequalities in One Variable
targets: I can graph the solution to an inequality in one variable.
I can solve one-variable inequalities and interpret the solutions in terms of the situation.
I understand that the solution to an inequality is a range of values (such as x\gt7) that makes the inequality true.

3.title: Writing and Solving Inequalities in One Variable
targets: I can analyze the structure of an inequality in one variable to help determine if the solution is greater or less than the solution to the related equation.
I can write and solve inequalities to answer questions about a situation.

4.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities in Two Variables (Part 1)
targets: Given a two-variable inequality and the graph of the related equation, I can determine on which side of the line the solutions to the inequality will fall.
I can describe the graph that represents the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables.

5.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities in Two Variables (Part 2)
targets: Given a two-variable inequality that represents a situation, I can interpret points in the coordinate plane and decide if they are solutions to the inequality.
I can find the solutions to a two-variable inequality by using the graph of a related two-variable equation.
I can write inequalities to describe the constraints in a situation.

6.title: Solving Problems with Inequalities in Two Variables
targets: I can use graphing technology to find the solution to a two-variable inequality.
When given inequalities, graphs, and descriptions that represent the constraints in a situation, I can connect the different representations and interpret them in terms of the situation.

7.title: Solutions to Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
targets: I can write a system of inequalities to describe a situation, find the solution by graphing, and interpret points in the solution.
I know what is meant by "the solutions to a system of inequalities" and can describe the graphs that represent the solutions.
When given descriptions and graphs that represent two different constraints, I can find values that satisfy each constraint individually, and values that satisfy both constraints at once.

8.title: Solving Problems with Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
targets: I can explain how to tell if a point on the boundary of the graph of the solutions to a system of inequalities is a solution or not.

9.title: Modeling with Systems of Inequalities in Two Variables
targets: I can interpret inequalities and graphs in a mathematical model.
I know how to choose variables, specify the constraints, and write inequalities to create a mathematical model.

1.title: Describing and Graphing Situations
targets: I can explain when a relationship between two quantities is a function.
I can identify independent and dependent variables in a function and use words and graphs to represent the function.
I can make sense of descriptions and graphs of functions and explain what they tell us about situations.

2.title: Function Notation
targets: I can use function notation to express functions that have specific inputs and outputs.
I understand what function notation is and why it exists.
When given a statement written in function notation, I can explain what it means in terms of a situation.

3.title: Interpreting and Using Function Notation
targets: I can describe the connections between a statement in function notation and the graph of the function.
I can use function notation to efficiently represent a relationship between two quantities in a situation.
I can use statements in function notation to sketch a graph of a function.

4.title: Using Function Notation to Describe Rules (Part 1)
targets: I can make sense of rules of functions when they are written in function notation, and create tables and graphs to represent the functions.
I can write equations that represent the rules of functions.

5.title: Using Function Notation to Describe Rules (Part 2)
targets: I can use technology to graph a function given in function notation and use the graph to find the values of the function.
I know different ways to find the value of a function and to solve equations written in function notation.
I know what makes a function a linear function.

6.title: Features of Graphs
targets: I can identify important features of graphs of functions and explain what they mean in the situations represented.
I understand and can use the terms “horizontal intercept,” “vertical intercept,” “maximum,” and “minimum” when talking about functions and their graphs.

7.title: Using Graphs to Find Average Rate of Change
targets: I understand the meaning of the term “average rate of change.”
When given a graph of a function, I can estimate or calculate the average rate of change between two points.

8.title: Interpreting and Creating Graphs
targets: I can explain the average rate of change of a function in terms of a situation.
I can make sense of important features of a graph and explain what they mean in a situation.
When given a description or a visual representation of a situation, I can sketch a graph that shows important features of the situation.

9.title: Comparing Graphs
targets: I can compare the features of graphs of functions and explain what they mean in the situations represented.
I can make sense of an equation of the form f(x)=g(x) in terms of a situation and a graph, and know how to find the solutions.

10.title: Domain and Range (Part 1)
targets: I know what is meant by the “domain” and “range” of a function.
When given a description of a function in a situation, I can determine a reasonable domain and range for the function.

11.title: Domain and Range (Part 2)
targets: When given a description of a function in a situation, I can determine a reasonable domain and range for the function.

12.title: Piecewise Functions
targets: I can make sense of a graph of a piecewise function in terms of a situation and sketch a graph of the function when the rules are given.
I can make sense of the rules of a piecewise function when they are written in function notation and explain what they mean in the situation represented.
I understand what makes a function a piecewise function.

13.title: Absolute Value Functions (Part 1)
targets: Given a set of numerical guesses and a target number, I can calculate absolute errors and create a scatter plot of the data.
I can analyze and describe features of a scatter plot that shows absolute error data.
I can describe the general relationship between guesses and absolute errors using words or equations.

14.title: Absolute Value Functions (Part 2)
targets: I can describe the effects of adding a number to the expression that defines an absolute value function.
I can explain the meaning of absolute value function in terms of distance.
When given an absolute value function in words or in function notation, I can make sense of it and create a table of values and a graph to represent it.

15.title: Inverse Functions
targets: I understand the meaning of “inverse function” and how it could be found.
When given a linear function that represents a situation, I can use words and equations to describe the inverse function.

16.title: Finding and Interpreting Inverse Functions
targets: I can explain the meaning of an inverse function in terms of a situation.
When I have an equation that defines a linear function, I know how to find its inverse.

17.title: Writing Inverse Functions to Solve Problems
targets: I can write a linear function to model given data and find the inverse of the function.
When given a linear function defined using function notation, I know how to find its inverse.

18.title: Using Functions to Model Battery Power
targets: I can write a function to describe a situation and make predictions.

1.title: Growing and Growing
targets: I can compare growth patterns using calculations and graphs.

2.title: Patterns of Growth
targets: I can use words and expressions to describe patterns in tables of values.
When I have descriptions of linear and exponential relationships, I can write expressions and create tables of values to represent them.

3.title: Representing Exponential Growth
targets: I can explain the connections between an equation and a graph that represents exponential growth.
I can write and interpret an equation that represents exponential growth.

4.title: Representing Exponential Decay
targets: I can explain the meanings of a and b in an equation that represents exponential decay and is written as y=a \boldcdot b^x.

5.title: Understanding Decay
targets: I can use only multiplication to represent "decreasing a quantity by a fraction of itself."
I can write an expression or equation to represent a quantity that decays exponentially.
I know the meanings of “exponential growth” and “exponential decay.”

6.title: Analyzing Graphs
targets: I can use graphs to compare and contrast situations that involve exponential decay.
I can use information from a graph to write an equation that represents exponential decay.

7.title: Using Negative Exponents
targets: I can describe the meaning of a negative exponent in equations that represent exponential decay.
I can write and graph an equation that represents exponential decay to solve problems.

8.title: Exponential Situations as Functions
targets: I can use function notation to write equations that represent exponential relationships.
When I see relationships in descriptions, tables, equations, or graphs, I can determine whether the relationships are functions.

9.title: Interpreting Exponential Functions
targets: I can analyze a situation and determine whether it makes sense to connect the points on the graph that represents the situation.
When I see a graph of an exponential function, I can make sense of and describe the relationship using function notation.

10.title: Looking at Rates of Change
targets: I can calculate the average rate of change of a function over a specified period of time.
I know how the average rate of change of an exponential function differs from that of a linear function.

12.title: Reasoning about Exponential Graphs (Part 1)
targets: I can describe the effect of changing a and b on a graph that represents f(x)=a \boldcdot b^x.
I can use equations and graphs to compare exponential functions.

13.title: Reasoning about Exponential Graphs (Part 2)
targets: I can explain the meaning of the intersection of the graphs of two functions in terms of the situations they represent.
When I know two points on a graph of an exponential function, I can write an equation for the function.

14.title: Recalling Percent Change
targets: I can find the result of applying a percent increase or decrease on a quantity.
I can write different expressions to represent a starting amount and a percent increase or decrease.

15.title: Functions Involving Percent Change
targets: I can use graphs to illustrate and compare different percent increases.
I can write a numerical expression or an algebraic expression to represent the result of applying a percent increase repeatedly.

16.title: Compounding Interest
targets: I can explain why applying a percent increase, p, n times is like or unlike applying the percent increase np.

17.title: Different Compounding Intervals
targets: I can calculate interest when I know the starting balance, interest rate, and compounding intervals.
When given interest rates and compounding intervals, I can choose the better investment option.

18.title: Expressed in Different Ways
targets: I can solve problems using exponential expressions written in different ways.
I can write equivalent expressions to represent situations that involve repeated percent increase or decrease.

19.title: Which One Changes Faster?
targets: I can use tables, calculations, and graphs to compare growth rates of linear and exponential functions and to predict how the quantities change eventually.

20.title: Changes over Equal Intervals
targets: I can calculate rates of change of functions given graphs, equations, or tables.
I can use rates of change to describe how a linear function and an exponential function change over equal intervals.

21.title: Predicting Populations
targets: I can determine how well a chosen model fits the given information.
I can determine whether to use a linear function or an exponential function to model real-world data.

1.title: A Different Kind of Change
targets: I can create drawings, tables, and graphs that represent the area of a garden.
I can recognize a situation represented by a graph that increases and then decreases.

2.title: How Does It Change?
targets: I can describe how a pattern is growing.
I can tell whether a pattern is growing linearly, exponentially, or quadratically.
I know a quadratic expression has a squared term.

3.title: Building Quadratic Functions from Geometric Patterns
targets: I can explain using graphs, tables, or calculations that exponential functions eventually grow faster than do quadratic functions.
I can recognize quadratic functions written in different ways.
I can use information from a pattern of shapes to write a quadratic function.

4.title: Comparing Quadratic and Exponential Functions
targets: I can explain using graphs, tables, or calculations that exponential functions eventually grow faster than do quadratic functions.

5.title: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 1)
targets: I can explain the meaning of the terms in a quadratic expression that represents the height of a falling object.
I can use tables, graphs, and equations to represent the height of a falling object.

6.title: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 2)
targets: I can create quadratic functions and graphs that represent a situation.
I can relate the vertex of a graph and the zeros of a function to a situation.
I know that the domain of a function can depend on the situation it represents.

7.title: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 3)
targets: I can choose a domain that makes sense in a revenue situation.
I can model revenue with quadratic functions and graphs.
I can relate the vertex of a graph and the zeros of a function to a revenue situation.

8.title: Equivalent Quadratic Expressions
targets: I can rewrite quadratic expressions in different forms by using an area diagram or the distributive property.

9.title: Standard Form and Factored Form
targets: I can rewrite quadratic expressions given in factored form in standard form, using either the distributive property or a diagram.
I know the difference between “factored form” and “standard form.”

10.title: Graphs of Functions in Standard and Factored Forms
targets: I can explain the meaning of the intercepts on a graph of a quadratic function in terms of the situation it represents.
I know how the numbers in the factored form of a quadratic expression relate to the intercepts of its graph.

11.title: Graphing from the Factored Form
targets: I can graph a quadratic function given in factored form.
I know how to find the vertex and y-intercept of the graph of a quadratic function in factored form without graphing it first.

12.title: Graphing the Standard Form (Part 1)
targets: I can explain how the a and c in y=ax^2+bx+c affect the graph of the equation.
I understand how graphs, tables, and equations that represent the same quadratic function are related.

13.title: Graphing the Standard Form (Part 2)
targets: I can explain how the b in y=ax^2+bx+c affects the graph of the equation.
I can match equations given in standard and factored form with their graph.

14.title: Graphs That Represent Situations
targets: I can explain how a quadratic equation and its graph relate to a situation.

15.title: Vertex Form
targets: I can recognize the “vertex form” of a quadratic equation.
I can relate the numbers in the vertex form of a quadratic equation to its graph.

16.title: Graphing from the Vertex Form
targets: I can graph a quadratic function given in vertex form, showing a maximum or minimum and the y-intercept.
I know how to find a maximum or a minimum of a quadratic function given in vertex form without first graphing it.

17.title: Changing the Vertex
targets: I can describe how changing a number in the vertex form of a quadratic function affects its graph.

1.title: Finding Unknown Inputs
targets: I can explain the meaning of a solution to an equation in terms of a situation.
I can write a quadratic equation that represents a situation.

2.title: When and Why Do We Write Quadratic Equations?
targets: I can recognize the factored form of a quadratic expression and know when it can be useful for solving problems.
I can use a graph to find the solutions to a quadratic equation but also know its limitations.

3.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Reasoning
targets: I can find solutions to quadratic equations by reasoning about the values that make the equation true.
I know that quadratic equations may have two solutions.

4.title: Solving Quadratic Equations with the Zero Product Property
targets: I can explain the meaning of the “zero product property.”
I can find solutions to quadratic equations when one side is a product of factors and the other side is zero.

5.title: How Many Solutions?
targets: I can explain why dividing by a variable to solve a quadratic equation is not a good strategy.
I know that quadratic equations can have no solutions and can explain why when there are none.

6.title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 1)
targets: I can explain how the numbers in a quadratic expression in factored form relate to the numbers in an equivalent expression in standard form.
When given quadratic expressions in factored form, I can rewrite them in standard form.
When given quadratic expressions in the form of x^2+bx+c, I can rewrite them in factored form.

7.title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 2)
targets: I can explain how the numbers and signs in a quadratic expression in factored form relate to the numbers and signs in an equivalent expression in standard form.
When given a quadratic expression given in standard form with a negative constant term, I can write an equivalent expression in factored form.

8.title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 3)
targets: I can explain why multiplying a sum and a difference, (x+m)(x-m), results in a quadratic expression with no linear term.

9.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Using Factored Form
targets: I can rearrange a quadratic equation to be written as an expression in factored form equal to zero and find the solutions.
I can recognize the number of solutions for a quadratic equation from the factored form.

10.title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 4)
targets: I can use the factored form of a quadratic expression or a graph of a quadratic function to answer questions about a situation.
When given quadratic expressions of the form ax^2+bx+c, where a is not 1, I can write equivalent expressions in factored form.

11.title: What Are Perfect Squares?
targets: I can recognize perfect-square expressions written in different forms.
I can recognize quadratic equations that have a perfect-square expression and solve the equations.

12.title: Completing the Square (Part 1)
targets: I can explain what it means to “complete the square” and describe how to do it.
I can solve quadratic equations by completing the square and finding square roots.

13.title: Completing the Square (Part 2)
targets: When given a quadratic equation in which the coefficient of the squared term is 1, I can solve it by completing the square.

14.title: Completing the Square (Part 3)
targets: I can complete the square for quadratic expressions of the form ax^2+bx+c, where a is not 1, and explain the process.
I can solve quadratic equations in which the squared term coefficient is not 1 by completing the square.

15.title: Quadratic Equations with Irrational Solutions
targets: I can use the radical and “plus-minus” symbols to represent solutions to quadratic equations.
I know why the plus-minus symbol is used when solving quadratic equations by finding square roots.

16.title: The Quadratic Formula
targets: I can use the quadratic formula to solve quadratic equations.
I know some methods for solving quadratic equations can be more convenient than others.

17.title: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 1)
targets: I can use the quadratic formula to solve an equation and interpret the solutions in terms of a situation.

18.title: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 2)
targets: I can identify common errors when using the quadratic formula.
I know some ways to tell if a number is a solution to a quadratic equation.

19.title: Deriving the Quadratic Formula
targets: I can explain the steps and complete some missing steps for deriving the quadratic formula.
I know how the quadratic formula is related to the process of completing the square for a quadratic equation ax^2+bx+c=0.

20.title: Rational and Irrational Solutions
targets: I can explain why adding a rational number and an irrational number produces an irrational number.
I can explain why multiplying a rational number (except 0) and an irrational number produces an irrational number.
I can explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational.

21.title: Sums and Products of Rational and Irrational Numbers
targets: I can explain why adding a rational number and an irrational number produces an irrational number.
I can explain why multiplying a rational number (except 0) and an irrational number produces an irrational number.
I can explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational.

22.title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Vertex Form
targets: I can identify the vertex of the graph of a quadratic function when the expression that defines it is written in vertex form.
I know the meaning of the term “vertex form” and can recognize examples of quadratic expressions written in this form.
When given a quadratic expression in standard form, I can rewrite it in vertex form.

23.title: Using Quadratic Expressions in Vertex Form to Solve Problems
targets: I can find the maximum or minimum of a function by writing, in vertex form, the quadratic expression that defines it.
When given a quadratic function in vertex form, I can explain why the vertex is a maximum or minimum.

24.title: Using Quadratic Equations to Model Situations and Solve Problems
targets: I can interpret information about a quadratic function given its equation or a graph.
I can rewrite quadratic functions in different but equivalent forms of my choosing and use that form to solve problems.
In situations modeled by quadratic functions, I can decide which form to use depending on the questions being asked.

1.title: Understanding Proportional Relationships
targets: I can graph a proportional relationship from a story.
I can use the constant of proportionality to compare the pace of different animals.

2.title: Graphs of Proportional Relationships
targets: I can graph a proportional relationship from an equation.
I can tell when two graphs are of the same proportional relationship even if the scales are different.

3.title: Representing Proportional Relationships
targets: I can scale and label coordinate axes in order to graph a proportional relationship.

4.title: Comparing Proportional Relationships
targets: I can compare proportional relationships represented in different ways.

5.title: Introduction to Linear Relationships
targets: I can find the rate of change of a linear relationship by figuring out the slope of the line representing the relationship.

6.title: More Linear Relationships
targets: I can interpret the vertical intercept of a graph of a real-world situation.
I can match graphs to the real-world situations they represent by identifying the slope and the vertical intercept.

7.title: Representations of Linear Relationships
targets: I can use patterns to write a linear equation to represent a situation.
I can write an equation for the relationship between the total volume in a graduated cylinder and the number of objects added to the graduated cylinder.

8.title: Translating to y=mx+b
targets: I can explain where to find the slope and vertical intercept in both an equation and its graph.
I can write equations of lines using y=mx+b.

9.title: Slopes Don't Have to Be Positive
targets: I can create a graph of a situation that has a negative slope.
I can determine if a situation or a graph has a slope that is positive, negative, or zero and explain how I know.

10.title: Calculating Slope
targets: I can calculate positive and negative slopes given two points on the line.

11.title: Line Designs
targets: I can describe a line precisely enough that another student can draw it.

12.title: Equations of All Kinds of Lines
targets: I can write equations of lines that have a positive or a negative slope.
I can write equations of vertical and horizontal lines.

13.title: Solutions to Linear Equations
targets: I know that the graph of an equation is a visual representation of all the solutions to the equation.
I understand what the solution to an equation in two variables is.

14.title: More Solutions to Linear Equations
targets: I can find solutions (x, y) to linear equations given either the x- or y-value to start from.

15.title: Using Linear Relations to Solve Problems
targets: I can write linear equations to reason about real-world situations.

1.title: Writing Equivalent Equations
targets: I can describe moves that change one equation into an equivalent equation.

2.title: Keeping the Equation Balanced
targets: I can add or remove blocks from a hanger and keep the hanger balanced.
I can represent balanced hangers with equations.

3.title: Balanced Moves
targets: I can add, subtract, multiply, or divide each side of an equation by the same expression to get a new equation with the same solution.

4.title: More Balanced Moves
targets: I can make sense of multiple ways to solve an equation.

5.title: Solving Any Linear Equation
targets: I can solve an equation where the variable appears on both sides.

6.title: Strategic Solving
targets: I can solve linear equations in one variable.

7.title: All, Some, or No Solutions
targets: I can determine whether an equation has no solutions, one solution, or infinitely many solutions.

8.title: How Many Solutions?
targets: I can solve equations with different numbers of solutions.

9.title: When Are They the Same?
targets: I can use an expression to find when two things, like height, are the same in a real-world situation.

10.title: On or Off the Line?
targets: I can identify ordered pairs that are solutions to an equation.
I can interpret ordered pairs that are solutions to an equation.

11.title: On Both of the Lines
targets: I can use graphs to find an ordered pair that two real-world situations have in common.

12.title: Systems of Equations
targets: I can explain the solution to a system of equations in a real-world context.
I can explain what a system of equations is.
I can make graphs to find an ordered pair that two real-world situations have in common.

13.title: Solving Systems of Equations
targets: I can graph a system of equations.
I can solve systems of equations using algebra.

14.title: Solving More Systems
targets: I can use the structure of equations to help me figure out how many solutions a system of equations has.

15.title: Writing Systems of Equations
targets: I can write a system of equations from a real-world situation.

16.title: Solving Problems with Systems of Equations
targets: I can use a system of equations to represent a real-world situation and answer questions about the situation.

1.title: Inputs and Outputs
targets: I can write rules when I know input-output pairs.
I know how an input-output diagram represents a rule.

2.title: Introduction to Functions
targets: I know that a function is a rule with exactly one output for each allowable input.
I know that if a rule has exactly one output for each allowable input, then the output depends on the input.

3.title: Equations for Functions
targets: I can find the output of a function when I know the input.
I can name the independent and dependent variables for a given function and represent the function with an equation.

4.title: Tables, Equations, and Graphs of Functions
targets: I can identify graphs that do, and do not, represent functions.
I can use a graph of a function to find the output for a given input and to find the input(s) for a given output.

5.title: More Graphs of Functions
targets: I can explain the story told by the graph of a function.

6.title: Even More Graphs of Functions
targets: I can draw the graph of a function that represents a real-world situation.

7.title: Connecting Representations of Functions
targets: I can compare inputs and outputs of functions that are represented in different ways.

8.title: Linear Functions
targets: I can determine whether a function is increasing or decreasing based on whether its rate of change is positive or negative.
I can explain in my own words how the graph of a linear function relates to its rate of change and initial value.

9.title: Linear Models
targets: I can decide when a linear function is a good model for data and when it is not.
I can use data points to model a linear function.

10.title: Piecewise Linear Functions
targets: I can create graphs of nonlinear functions with pieces of linear functions.

11.title: Filling Containers
targets: I can collect data about a function and represent it as a graph.
I can describe the graph of a function in words.

12.title: How Much Will Fit?
targets: I know that volume is the amount of space contained inside a three-dimensional figure.
I recognize the following three-dimensional shapes: cylinder, cone, rectangular prism, and sphere.

13.title: The Volume of a Cylinder
targets: I can find the volume of a cylinder in mathematical and real-world situations.
I know the formula for volume of a cylinder.

14.title: Finding Cylinder Dimensions
targets: I can find missing information about a cylinder if I know its volume and some other information.

15.title: The Volume of a Cone
targets: I can find the volume of a cone in mathematical and real-world situations.
I know the formula for the volume of a cone.

16.title: Finding Cone Dimensions
targets: I can find missing information about a cone if I know its volume and some other information.

17.title: Scaling One Dimension
targets: I can create a graph of the relationship between volume and height for all cylinders and cones with a fixed radius.
I can explain in my own words why changing the height by a scale factor changes the volume by the same scale factor.

18.title: Scaling Two Dimensions
targets: I can create a graph representing the relationship between volume and radius for all cones (or cylinders) with a fixed height.
I can explain in my own words why changing the radius by a scale factor changes the volume by the scale factor squared.

19.title: Estimating a Hemisphere
targets: I can estimate the volume of a hemisphere by calculating the volume of a shape I know is larger and the volume of a shape I know is smaller.

20.title: The Volume of a Sphere
targets: I can find the volume of a sphere when I know the radius.

21.title: Cylinders, Cones, and Spheres
targets: I can find the radius of a sphere if I know its volume.
I can solve mathematical and real-world problems about the volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

22.title: Volume as a Function of...
targets: I can compare functions about volume represented in different ways.

1.title: Organizing Data
targets: I can organize data to see patterns more clearly.

2.title: Plotting Data
targets: I can draw a scatter plot to show data that has two paired variables.

3.title: What a Point in a Scatter Plot Means
targets: I can describe the meaning of a point in a scatter plot in context.

4.title: Fitting a Line to Data
targets: I can pick out outliers on a scatter plot.
I can use a model to predict values for data.

5.title: Describing Trends in Scatter Plots
targets: I can draw a line to fit data in a scatter plot.
I can say whether data in a scatter plot has a positive or negative association (or neither).

6.title: The Slope of a Fitted Line
targets: I can use the slope of a line fit to data in a scatter plot to say how the variables are connected in real-world situations.

7.title: Observing More Patterns in Scatter Plots
targets: I can pick out clusters in data from a scatter plot.
I can use a scatter plot to decide if two variables have a linear association.

8.title: Analyzing Bivariate Data
targets: I can analyze a set of data to determine associations between two variables.

9.title: Looking for Associations
targets: I can identify the same data represented in a bar graph, a segmented bar graph, and a two-way table.
I can use a two-way frequency table or relative frequency table to find associations among variables.

10.title: Using Data Displays to Find Associations
targets: I can create relative frequency tables, bar graphs, and segmented bar graphs from frequency tables to find associations among variables.

11.title: Gone in 30 Seconds
targets: I can collect data and analyze it for associations using scatter plots, two-way tables, and segmented bar graphs.
